title: Agent Stream Name Drift (Mistyped Stream Opens an Empty Stream)
dataSources: `SPLUNK_AO_AGENT_STREAM` in each deployment's environment and the stream read-back from `AgentStream.get(name=..., project_name=...)`
description: Detects agents logging to the wrong Agent Stream. Stream names are case-sensitive and logging to a name that does not exist creates it, so one typo sends traces to a new, empty stream with no evaluators or alerts.
value: Keeps traces in the stream where evaluators, alerts and controls are configured. A mistyped stream looks healthy from the agent side while the real stream goes quiet and every quality check on it stops.
implementation: Set `SPLUNK_AO_AGENT_STREAM` from deployment configuration, never from code. After each deploy, read the expected stream back with `AgentStream.get` and confirm recent traces arrived. Replace any use of the deprecated `SPLUNK_AO_LOG_STREAM` alias.
visualization: Project stream list in the console; deploy check result per environment.
knownFalsePositives: A brand-new environment's stream is empty until its first request. Run the read-back after the first smoke-test request, and allow 30 to 60 seconds of indexing lag.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites

A Splunk Agent Observability project for the application and one Agent Stream per environment or agent inside it. Do not create a second project for the same application: a second project splits the traces. The agent reads `SPLUNK_AO_PROJECT` and `SPLUNK_AO_AGENT_STREAM` from the environment. SaaS tenants authenticate with `SPLUNK_AO_REALM` and `SPLUNK_AO_O11Y_TOKEN`; on-prem tenants with `SPLUNK_AO_API_KEY` plus `SPLUNK_AO_CONSOLE_URL`. Install the SDK with `pip install splunk-ao` (`pip install "splunk-ao[langchain]"` for the LangChain callback).

Step 1 — Instrument the agent

The console says Agent Stream; the SDK and REST API still say log stream (`log_stream_id`). They are the same object. The SDK reads `SPLUNK_AO_AGENT_STREAM`; `SPLUNK_AO_LOG_STREAM` is a deprecated alias.

Step 2 — Configure in Splunk Agent Observability

In the project, list the Agent Streams and look for near-duplicate names (case or spelling variants). Evaluators, alerts and sampling are set per stream, so a variant stream has none of them.

Step 3 — Validate

Run the post-deploy check after a smoke-test request. To check from code instead of the console, read the stream back with `AgentStream.get(name=stream_name, project_name=project_name)` and call `get_traces(limit=5)` or `get_spans(limit=20)`. Indexing lag is 30 to 60 seconds, so an empty result right after a run is not proof of failure. This use case was written from the Splunk Agent Observability documentation without access to a tenant, so it ships as a draft. Confirm each step in the Splunk Agent Observability console before promoting it.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add the check to the deployment pipeline for every environment. Keep stream names in one configuration file per environment.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

Traces in a stream nobody configured: compare the exact, case-sensitive value of `SPLUNK_AO_AGENT_STREAM` in that deployment with the stream that has the evaluators. Move the agent back by fixing the variable; the stray stream keeps its traces.
grandmaExplanation: We make sure the assistant files its notes in the right drawer, because a misspelled drawer name quietly creates a new, empty drawer.

productArtifacts.title: Post-deploy check that traces reach the expected stream
productArtifacts.body:
import os
from splunk_ao import AgentStream

stream_name = os.environ["SPLUNK_AO_AGENT_STREAM"]
project_name = os.environ["SPLUNK_AO_PROJECT"]

s = AgentStream.get(name=stream_name, project_name=project_name)
recent = s.get_traces(limit=5)
assert len(recent) > 0, f"no traces in {project_name}/{stream_name}; check the stream name"
